title: Visualizing surface-reaction-driven chloride migration and cascading failure in sulfide solid electrolytes
abstract: Moisture instability of sulfide solid electrolytes limits practical use in all-solid-state batteries. Spatially resolving gas--solid reactions during moisture exposure remains challenging. Here, cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (cryo-4D-STEM) maps nanoscale degradation in low- and high-Cl argyrodite electrolytes, Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl and Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\). Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl undergoes predominantly surface-localized degradation that progressively extends inward, whereas Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\) exhibits rapid interior amorphization accompanied by outward chloride redistribution. Density functional theory calculations indicate a lower chloride-migration barrier along the modeled pathway in the higher-Cl composition, while chloride removal and vacancy formation distort the PS\(_4^{3-}\) framework and may destabilize the lattice. Surface treatment suppresses detectable large-scale chloride segregation and improves moisture tolerance, retaining 99.9% of the capacity measured at the start of 0.33 C cycling after 150 cycles. These results identify chloride redistribution as a key process in degradation propagation and suggest a route toward moisture-tolerant solid-state batteries.

title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.

title: Light-induced local control of magnetic anisotropy and domain pattern in Co/Pt multilayers
abstract: Control of magnetic anisotropy is essential for the fabrication of next-generation devices in spintronics and magnetic memory. While conventional approaches such as material composition, thermal annealing, and ion bombardment are widely used, achieving spatially resolved, continuous control remains a challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a dual-regime, localized control over both transient magnetic states and permanent intrinsic properties in perpendicularly magnetized Co/Pt multilayers using ultra-short laser pulses. By employing a multi-scale approach combining Kerr microscopy, magnetic force microscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry, we reveal that low-fluence irradiation enables a reversible, helicity-dependent accumulation of magnetic phases without altering the intrinsic quasistatic properties. Conversely, high-fluence exposure acts as localized thermal annealing that permanently hardens the magnetic system. This structural relaxation leads to a substantial enhancement of the effective perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, driving a twofold increase in the local coercive field and expanding the equilibrium stripe domain width. By offering both reversible spin manipulation and deterministic engineering of 2D magnetic landscapes, this work paves the way towards flexible, lithography-free anisotropy structuring for advanced spintronic applications.

summaries.en: Ultra-short laser pulses provide dual-regime local control of perpendicularly magnetized Co/Pt multilayers, where low fluence reversibly accumulates helicity-dependent magnetic phases without changing intrinsic quasistatic properties, while high fluence acts as localized thermal annealing that permanently enhances effective perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, doubling the local coercive field and widening equilibrium stripe domains.

title: Kinematics of Inverse Compton Scattering from Dirac Carriers in Graphene
abstract: We examine the kinematics of Compton and inverse Compton scattering by Dirac carriers in graphene. Unlike photons in vacuum, which propagate at the speed of light c, graphene carriers have a characteristic velocity vF, with vF much less than c. This difference means that the standard Compton scattering formula cannot be applied to graphene simply by replacing c with vF. We first examine Compton-like scattering for a gapless Dirac carrier initially at the Dirac point and for a gapped carrier at the band edge, both corresponding to zero in-plane momentum. We then consider scattering from an energetic gapless Dirac carrier. By combining energy conservation with the graphene dispersion and in-plane momentum conservation, we obtain a quadratic equation for the scattered photon energy within the model considered. This relation is the main kinematic result of the work. We identify inverse Compton-like scattering by the transfer of energy from the carrier to the photon, subject to the simultaneous conservation of energy and in-plane momentum. We also discuss how this process differs kinematically from Doppler-shifted emission, Cerenkov-like radiation, harmonic generation, photon drag, and other nonlinear optical processes. Finally, we propose a time-resolved pump-probe arrangement in which the scattered photon spectrum is the primary observable, while time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) provides an independent probe of the nonequilibrium carrier distribution. These results provide a kinematic framework for analysing inverse Compton-like scattering in graphene and for identifying the conditions under which energy can be transferred from energetic Dirac carriers to photons.

summaries.en: This work derives a kinematic framework for Compton and inverse Compton-like scattering by Dirac carriers in graphene, showing that the carriers' Fermi velocity vF < c invalidates a simple replacement of c with vF and yielding a quadratic equation for the scattered photon energy from energy and in-plane momentum conservation, distinguishing the process from Doppler-shifted emission, Cerenkov-like radiation, harmonic generation, and photon drag.

title: Magnetic order in epitaxial (La2/3Sr1/3MnO3)3/(BaTiO3)3 trilayer heterostructures: Evidence for quasi-two-dimensional ferrimagnetism
abstract: The realization of artificial magnetic structures with high epitaxial quality and elevated critical temperatures remains a key challenge for spintronics. Here, we report the fabrication and characterization of epitaxial (La2/3Sr1/3MnO3)3/(BaTiO3)3 trilayer heterostructures grown by layer-by-layer laser ablation. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy, magnetization measurements, and neutron diffraction confirm their exceptional crystalline order and the absence of structural defects. Neutron diffraction reveals no antiferromagnetic Bragg peaks, ruling out most antiferromagnetic configurations with a non zero wave vector Q. Magnetic hysteresis loops instead evidence a ferromagnetic order with a remanent moment of about 0.5 bohr magneton per Mn atom at room temperature, persisting either in-plane or out-of-plane depending on the applied field. Our findings highlight neutron diffraction as a powerful tool for elucidating the magnetic structure of complex thin films and suggest that weak interlayer coupling through BaTiO3 leads to ferromagnetism with a high critical temperature (about 600 K).

title: Oxygen on Rh(100) revisited with ultra-high precision
abstract: We have reanalyzed the 0.25 and 0.50 monolayer (ML) phases of oxygen on the catalytically important Rh(100) surface by quantitative low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), variable-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and density functional theory (DFT). For both phases, the crystallographic structure could be determined by LEED structure analyses with single-digit picometer precision enabled by ultra-low Pendry R factors of R$_\mathrm{P}$ $\approx$ 0.07. For the (2$\times$2)-O phase at 0.25 ML we find oxygen adsorbed at fourfold hollow sites in accordance to earlier results [Surf. Sci. 207 (1988) 55], however, with a pronounced buckling within the second layer of the otherwise unreconstructed substrate. For the 0.50 monolayer phase, we recently identified a (2$\sqrt{2}$ $\times$ 2$\sqrt{2}$)R45$^\circ$-4O ground state structure [Phys. Rev. Res. 8 (2026) 023296], which decomposes into a large number of nano-domains already at temperatures below 100 K. In this paper we provide a detailed analysis of the atomic structure and the ordering behavior of this phase and resolve long-standing discrepancies with the original (2$\times$2)pg model [Phys. Rev. Lett. 82 (1999) 4874]. We further prove by short-range order simulations that the coherent superposition of scattering contributions of the nano-domains leads to a virtual extinction of diffraction spots, which has concealed the true periodicity and symmetry of this phase for so long.

title: Analysis of Transient Microscopy Data in Reciprocal Space
abstract: Transient microscopy has evolved to include a family of well-established techniques for studying the spatiotemporal dynamics of excited states in a variety of materials systems. In these methods, a laser pulse is focused to locally excite a material, and the subsequent evolution of the excited species is visualized to extract transport parameters such as diffusivities. Typically, transport coefficients are extracted from experimental datasets using curve-fitting methods to analyze the change in the mean squared displacement (MSD) of the spatial profiles over time. However, this approach can lead to inaccurate or misleading diffusivity values under many common experimental conditions, and is only formally accurate for the case of a single diffusing species. In this work, we introduce a new approach to the analysis of transient microscopy data based on the evolution of profile shapes in reciprocal space. We use simulated datasets to quantitatively analyze the performance of our proposed methods and compare them to current state-of-the-art analysis techniques. We demonstrate that reciprocal-space-based analysis methods have the highest overall performance in terms of accuracy and precision for normal diffusive transport over a range of realistic initial conditions and signal-to-noise ratios. Furthermore, we highlight the limitations of using MSD alone to characterize anomalous transport in materials, and we show how analysis of spatial frequencies can yield a more comprehensive understanding of complex excited-state dynamics and their underlying physical mechanisms. Our results show that reciprocal-space-based analysis methods are powerful tools for characterizing and quantifying many different types of transport behaviors.

summaries.en: This work introduces reciprocal-space analysis of transient microscopy data, showing through simulations that it outperforms mean-squared-displacement fitting for accuracy and precision in normal diffusion and provides a more comprehensive characterization of anomalous transport and complex excited-state dynamics.

title: Limits from nonlinear loss of spin-orbit-torque control of magnon transport
abstract: Controlling magnon currents is central to the development of magnonic devices, which exploit spin excitations for information transport without charge flow. Here, we use the spin-orbit torque (SOT) from a Pt gate to control the effective magnon damping in three-terminal devices fabricated from low-damping lithium aluminum ferrite (LAFO) thin films and identify the nonlinear damping that ultimately limits the gate response. With increasing gate current, the nonlocal magnon signal initially increases, but saturates and subsequently decreases above a critical gate current density. Brillouin light scattering microscopy reveals that this turnover coincides with the emergence of an SOT-driven auto-oscillation mode localized beneath the gate, whose frequency continuously redshifts with increasing gate current, characteristic of large-amplitude nonlinear dynamics, and with a suppression of the propagating magnon population away from the gate. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the observed nonmonotonic gate response only when an amplitude-dependent effective damping is included, indicating that nonlinear losses, rather than saturation of spin injection, limit the degree of magnon modulation. Our results show that SOT compensation of magnon damping is ultimately limited by nonlinear damping attributed to auto-oscillations, providing a framework for understanding the limits of magnon current modulation in magnetic insulators.

summaries.en: Spin-orbit torque from a Pt gate can compensate magnon damping in low-damping lithium aluminum ferrite three-terminal devices, but the nonlocal magnon signal saturates and then decreases above a critical gate current density because SOT-driven auto-oscillations localized beneath the gate produce nonlinear damping that ultimately limits the gate response.

title: Noise Correlation Spectroscopy: A Review
abstract: The frequency noise of an ordinary diode laser, often a nuisance in spectroscopy, can be used to measure atomic coherence. When atoms are prepared in a coherent superposition of two ground states, each random shift in laser frequency changes how much light they absorb, so the transmitted light carries a record of that coherence. Correlating the intensity fluctuations of two fields, each linking one ground state to a shared excited state, reads this record out, a technique known as noise correlation spectroscopy. The correlation signal is narrower than the transparency window the same fields create and switches sign as their frequency difference is tuned. Its width is set by the rate at which the atoms lose coherence and, over a wide range, does not grow with laser power. Over two decades the method has spread from warm vapors to cold atoms, to multi-field schemes, and to diamond and rare-earth-doped crystals. This review, to the author's knowledge the first, brings together its theory, experiments and applications, and examines its limits, the challenges that remain, and the opportunities that could make it a standard spectroscopic tool.

summaries.en: This review surveys noise correlation spectroscopy, a technique that uses laser frequency noise to read out atomic coherence via intensity correlations between two fields coupled to a shared excited state, yielding a signal narrower than the induced transparency window and insensitive to laser power over a wide range, and covers its theory, experiments, and applications from warm vapors to cold atoms, multi-field schemes, diamond, and rare-earth-doped crystals.

title: Two-photon Doppler-free spectroscopy of the $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6s23s\;^1S_0$ Rydberg transition for quantum sensing in ytterbium
abstract: Here we report atomic structure calculations and experimental observations of the two-photon $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6s23s\;^1S_0$ transition in Yb. The unique level structure of Yb places the $6s6p\;^1P_1$ state's energy at $\approx\!49.7\%$ of the ionization energy, which facilitates two-photon Doppler-free excitation of the $6s23s\;^1S_0$ Rydberg state from the $6s^2\;^1S_0$ ground state at a relatively low optical intensity. This $J= 0 \rightarrow J=0$ transition is immune to first-order Zeeman and electric quadrupole shifts, has reduced sensitivity to higher-order Zeeman shifts, and is further predicted to have relatively low sensitivity to density shifts. Using configuration interaction theory, we compute relevant properties of the $6s23s\;^1S_0$ Rydberg state for sensing, including the $C_6$ coefficient, dc polarizability, blackbody radiation (BBR) shift, and BBR depopulation rate. As a first experimental step, we demonstrate two-photon Doppler-free spectroscopy of the $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6s23s\;^1S_0$ transition. From our experimental spectra, we estimate the natural linewidth (lifetime) of the $6s23s\;^1S_0$ state to be 90 kHz (1.8 $\mu$s). We believe this transition, or other $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6sns\;^1S_0$ transitions in Yb with $n\approx23$, may find use in a variety of sensing applications, potentially including a two-photon clock, electrometer, or BBR thermometer.

title: Ultra-stable laser with sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth using a silicon photonic chip
abstract: Here, we demonstrate a novel optical self-injection-locking scheme integrated with a modulation-free laser frequency stabilization technique co-integrated with a compact vacuum-gap micro-Fabry-Perot cavity (uFP), with Q-factor of 3.46E9, to realize an ultra-stable laser with sub-Hz fundamental linewidth using a silicon photonic chip. The demonstrated electro-optic self-injection locking (EOSIL) chip suppresses a commercial DFB diode laser's frequency noise power spectral density by more than 110 dB at 1 Hz offset, approaching the theoretical thermal noise limit of the uFP cavity, and enables a laser fundamental linewidth of 58 mHz with a fractional frequency instability of 8.68E-13 at 1 sec averaging time. The chip is fabricated using the Advanced Micro Foundry standard silicon photonic process and occupies a footprint of 10 mm^2.

title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $\mu$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

title: Time-Domain Data-Driven Loewner Reduced-Order Models for Electromagnetic Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven Loewner framework for constructing reduced-order models (ROMs) from time-domain electromagnetic (EM) simulation data. High-fidelity simulation of microwave devices can be computationally expensive, particularly when fine spatial discretization and long observation windows are required. The proposed method uses transient input-output data to construct Loewner and shifted Loewner matrices, from which a reduced descriptor realization is obtained through singular value decomposition (SVD). The resulting models are identified from a limited training window and used to predict responses over substantially longer time intervals, with prediction windows up to 50 times the duration of the training window. The method is formalized as an explicit, reproducible algorithm and validated against full-order simulations for four microwave structures: a substrate-integrated-waveguide filter, a frequency-selective surface, an evanescent-mode coaxial comb-line filter, and a diplexer. The results demonstrate the potential of Loewner-based identification to provide compact models of electromagnetic responses while reducing the need for repeated full-order simulation.

summaries.en: This paper introduces a data-driven Loewner framework that constructs reduced-order models from time-domain electromagnetic simulation data and predicts responses over windows up to 50 times the training duration, validated on four microwave structures including a substrate-integrated-waveguide filter, frequency-selective surface, evanescent-mode coaxial comb-line filter, and diplexer.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种数据驱动的Loewner框架，利用时域电磁仿真数据构建降阶模型，预测窗口可达训练窗口时长的50倍，并在基片集成波导滤波器、频率选择表面、倏逝模同轴梳状滤波器和双工器四种微波结构上得到验证。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、時間領域電磁界シミュレーションデータから低次元化モデルを構築するデータ駆動型Loewnerフレームワークを提案し、学習窓の最大50倍の期間にわたる応答予測を可能にするとともに、基板集積導波路フィルタ、周波数選択表面、エバネッセントモード同軸コムラインフィルタ、ダイプレクサの4つのマイクロ波構造で検証している。

title: Development of a fabrication-to-benchtop process for SiN-based quantum devices
abstract: Silicon nitride has emerged as a key material for the advancement of future quantum communication and computational devices. However, challenges persist in establishing a comprehensive development process, spanning from fabrication to optical characterization, essential for advancing these devices to their next stage of potential. Maintaining control over the entire process, from start to finish, alongside device modeling, enables more efficient and timely iteration and optimization. Here we introduce a fabrication-to-benchtop process. We employ an in-house stoichiometric recipe for device fabrication and conduct comprehensive characterization of optical losses and material properties. Understanding and controlling the refractive index of the device are vital for predicting device geometries and group indices. Implementing the refractive indices of our fabricated devices, we simulate microring resonators and demonstrate their application in generating optical solitons.

summaries.en: This work presents an end-to-end fabrication-to-benchtop process for silicon nitride quantum devices, using an in-house stoichiometric recipe, comprehensive characterization of optical losses and material properties, and refractive-index-informed simulations of microring resonators for optical soliton generation.
summaries.zh: 本工作提出了一套从制造到台式测试的氮化硅量子器件全流程工艺，采用自研的化学计量配方，全面表征光学损耗和材料特性，并利用实测折射率模拟微环谐振器以产生光孤子。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、独自の化学量論的レシピを用いた作製からベンチトップ測定までの窒化シリコン量子デバイスの一貫プロセスを提示し、光学損失と材料特性の包括的な評価、および実測屈折率に基づく微小リング共振器のシミュレーションによる光ソリトン生成を示した。

title: Programming the Nonlinear Optics of a Nanoporous Photonic Metamaterial by Confined Crystallization
abstract: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. Here each nanochannel is turned into a nonlinear optical meta-atom by filling anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) with benzil (BZL), a noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal, and the crystallization pathway programs their orientation. In free-standing membranes every channel solidifies independently, the orientations remain uncorrelated, and the effective second-harmonic generation (SHG) response is nearly polarization isotropic; its magnitude follows a core - shell model in which an optically inactive interfacial layer of 2.6 nm reduces the active volume of each meta-atom, reproducing on bare alumina the value previously found on alkyl-grafted silica and indicating a host-insensitive limit. Seeding crystallization from a bulk benzil layer instead aligns the meta-atoms over submillimeter domains and produces a macroscopically anisotropic effective susceptibility. Channel diameters from 32 to 270 nm span the transition out of the subwavelength regime, and the anomalous directional SHG emission reported here is confined to the metamaterial limit. Confined crystallization thus offers a route to nonlinear optical metamaterials whose effective susceptibility tensor is written during processing.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

summaries.en: Filling the nanochannels of an anodic aluminum oxide membrane with the noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal benzil turns each channel into a nonlinear optical meta-atom, and the crystallization pathway—independent solidification yielding near-isotropic second-harmonic generation versus bulk-seeded alignment producing macroscopic anisotropy—programs the effective susceptibility tensor of the resulting photonic metamaterial.
summaries.zh: 在阳极氧化铝膜的纳米通道中填充非中心对称分子晶体联苯甲酰，可将每个通道转变为非线性光学超原子，而结晶路径——独立固化产生近各向同性的二次谐波产生，或体相籽晶诱导排列产生宏观各向异性——编程了所得光子超材料的有效极化率张量。
summaries.ja: 陽極酸化アルミナ膜のナノチャネルに非中心対称分子結晶であるベンジルを充填することで各チャネルを非線形光学メタ原子とし、結晶化経路（独立固化によるほぼ等方的な第二高調波発生か、バルクからのシード結晶化による巨視的な異方性）が得られるフォトニックメタマテリアルの有効感受率テンソルをプログラムする。

title: Low-Cost Third-order Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Method for Excited States Using Tensor Hypercontraction and State-Specific Frozen Natural Orbitals
abstract: We have developed a reduced-cost framework for excited-state calculations by combining the state-specific frozen natural orbital (SS-FNO) approach with the third-order algebraic diagrammatic construction [ADC(3)] method and tensor hypercontraction (THC). This strategy enables a systematic and controllable truncation of the virtual orbital space, while significantly lowering the computational scaling through the THC representation of the electron repulsion integrals. The method allows black-box application via adjustable thresholds and includes a perturbative correction that compensates for the truncation error. We have used the CIS(D) method to generate the natural orbitals for the excited states. The performance of the SS-FNO-THC-ADC(3) method is assessed for valence, Rydberg, and charge-transfer excitations. Benchmark calculations demonstrate that the combined approach achieves excellent agreement with the canonical ADC(3) results. The efficiency of the present implementation is demonstrated by calculating the excitation energy of a molecule containing 31 atoms and more than one thousand basis functions.

summaries.en: The authors combine state-specific frozen natural orbitals with tensor hypercontraction to reduce the cost of third-order algebraic diagrammatic construction excited-state calculations, achieving excellent agreement with canonical ADC(3) results and demonstrating efficiency on a 31-atom system with over one thousand basis functions.
summaries.zh: 作者将态特定冻结自然轨道与张量超收缩相结合，降低了三阶代数图解构造激发态计算的成本，其结果与正则ADC(3)结果高度一致，并在一个含31个原子、超过一千个基函数的体系上展示了效率。
summaries.ja: 著者らは状態特異的凍結自然軌道とテンソル超縮約を組み合わせることで三次代数図式構成法による励起状態計算のコストを削減し、正準ADC(3)の結果と極めて良く一致するとともに、31原子・1000基底関数超の系で効率性を示した。

title: Thermalization-induced self-polarization of temporally incoherent light: A nonequilibrium wave turbulence kinetic approach
abstract: Conservative nonlinear waves generally undergo an irreversible process of thermalization toward the Rayleigh--Jeans (RJ) equilibrium state. Light thermalization has recently been experimentally investigated in the two-dimensional transverse spatial dynamics of multimode waveguides. Here, we consider the one-dimensional temporal dynamics of incoherent light propagating in a weakly birefringent single-mode fiber. We show that light thermalization is responsible for a self-polarization of the incoherent wave during its propagation. Within the framework of wave turbulence theory, we show that this phenomenon originates from a nonequilibrium process of adiabatic cooling: polarization fluctuations are continuously transferred toward the high-frequency tails of a local RJ equilibrium state, whose effective temperature decreases during propagation, thereby increasing the degree of light polarization. Moreover, in the absence of a high-frequency cut-off that would regularize the ultraviolet catastrophe in the temporal domain, the optical wave exhibits an ever-increasing degree of polarization, ultimately approaching unity. These results show that it is thermodynamically advantageous for the optical field to evolve toward a polarized state, which provides new insight into spontaneous self-organization phenomena in conservative Hamiltonian systems operating far from thermodynamic equilibrium.

summaries.en: Within wave turbulence theory, thermalization of temporally incoherent light in a weakly birefringent single-mode fiber drives self-polarization through adiabatic cooling, in which polarization fluctuations are continuously transferred to the high-frequency tails of a local Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium whose effective temperature decreases during propagation, so that the degree of polarization grows without bound and approaches unity when no high-frequency cutoff regularizes the ultraviolet catastrophe.
summaries.zh: 在波湍流理论框架下，弱双折射单模光纤中时间非相干光的热化通过绝热冷却导致自偏振：偏振涨落不断转移到局域瑞利-金斯平衡态的高频尾部，而该平衡态的有效温度随传输而降低，从而使偏振度持续增大，并在不存在高频截断以正则化紫外灾难时最终趋近于1。
summaries.ja: 波動乱流理論の枠組みにおいて、弱複屈折単一モードファイバー中の時間的に非干渉な光の熱化は断熱冷却を通じて自己偏光を引き起こし、偏光揺らぎが局所的なレイリー・ジーンズ平衡状態の高周波尾部へ連続的に移動し、その有効温度が伝搬中に低下することで偏光度が増大し、紫外破綻を正則化する高周波遮断が存在しない場合には偏光度が1に近づく。

title: Wavelength Diversity Expands the Expressive Power of Optical Computing
abstract: Universal function approximation underpins neural networks' capacity to represent nonlinear relationships, but realizing this capability in optical hardware requires engineering the computational features encoded in light. Here, we show that wavelength diversity enhances optical function-approximation expressivity through wavelength-scaled Fourier features generated by a shared phase encoder, without increasing the number of input-encoded harmonics. Multiple wavelengths contribute to the representation of each output function rather than merely serving as independent computational channels. We establish theoretical scaling laws and approximation-error bounds, revealing that, for nondispersive encoders, the spectral endpoints determine the accessible computational bandwidth, while intermediate illumination wavelengths enrich the available harmonics within that bandwidth. Numerical studies demonstrate improved approximation of real- and complex-valued nonlinear functions, with a representative design achieving more than a 100-fold reduction in mean-squared error relative to tested monochromatic optical processors with the same number of trainable phase features. Experimentally, we validate enhanced approximation accuracy and demonstrate the simultaneous approximation of 4,136 distinct nonlinear functions using a compact, single-layer diffractive processor under five-wavelength illumination. These results establish wavelength diversity as an additional physical resource for scaling the expressive power of optical computing and enhancing the accuracy of parallel nonlinear function approximation.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Neural and Evolutionary Computing (cs.NE); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph)

summaries.en: Wavelength diversity enhances the expressive power of optical computing by using a shared phase encoder to generate wavelength-scaled Fourier features, enabling a single-layer diffractive processor to simultaneously approximate 4,136 nonlinear functions under five-wavelength illumination and reducing mean-squared error by more than 100-fold compared with monochromatic processors.
summaries.zh: 波长多样性通过共享相位编码器生成波长缩放的傅里叶特征来增强光学计算的表现力，使单层衍射处理器在五波长照明下可同时逼近4,136个非线性函数，并将均方误差较单色处理器降低100倍以上。
summaries.ja: 波長多様性は共有位相エンコーダが生成する波長スケールのフーリエ特徴を通じて光学計算の表現力を高め、単層回折プロセッサが5波長照明下で4,136個の非線形関数を同時に近似することを可能にし、単色プロセッサと比べて平均二乗誤差を100倍以上低減する。

title: A dry cryogenic platform with picometre stability for nanoscale and quantum technologies
abstract: Mechanically ultrastable environments within maintenance-free dry cryostats are needed for high-precision surface probe microscopy experiments, as well as next-generation quantum technologies. The most demanding applications require picometre-scale precision combined with multi-axis and millimetre-scale scanning range, while offering access to optical, microwave, and radiofrequency control and a vector magnetic field. We demonstrate a versatile platform for such systems based on passive and active vibration control for a commercial dry cryostat. Using a tunable optical microcavity as a sensor, we report vibration levels of 4.2 pm root mean square at 2.3 K over one hour without postselection. We further demonstrate drift-free long-term operation with stability below 8.6 pm RMS over 12 hours. Our system enables continuous and automated operation for next-generation high-throughput applications without the need for liquid helium infrastructure. Requiring only standard machining facilities and commercially available hardware, the design can be readily adapted for cryogenic optical, electrical and magnetic high-precision measurements across quantum science, surface science, and nanotechnology.

title: Vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy via cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory
abstract: We derive a vibro-polaritonic Raman activity from third-order cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory (CBO-PT) accounting for weak interactions between electrons and low-frequency cavity modes in the vibrational strong coupling (VSC) regime. This work extends the recently presented CBO-PT linear response approach [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2024, 15, 2262-2269] from infrared (IR) to vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy. In a first step, we discuss cavity-induced corrections to the static dipole polarizability tensor, which manifest as molecular and cavity mode contribution determined by the polarization-projected static hyperpolarizability tensor. We then obtain the corresponding vibro-polaritonic Raman activity in double harmonic approximation, which contains molecular, cavity and mixed contributions similar to previously discussed CBO-PT IR intensities. The cavity Raman activity can be interpreted as effective transmission component, which is exclusively determined by the polaritonic Raman response. The methodology and its relation to vibro-polaritonic IR spectroscopy is illustrated for a formaldehyde molecule under VSC. An implementation of the CBO-PT linear response approach for vibro-polaritonic Raman and IR spectroscopies is provided via the open-source Python package CBOvibSpec.

summaries.en: The authors extend cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory to derive vibro-polaritonic Raman activities, including molecular, cavity, and mixed contributions, and demonstrate the approach for formaldehyde under vibrational strong coupling.

title: A compact, dual-colour chirped-pulse laser system for field-deployable coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering diagnostics
abstract: Single-shot coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering (CRBS) requires dual colour, frequency, and pulse duration agile laser systems, currently available only in laboratory layouts. In this work, we present a compact, portable, and robust next generation laser system that meets all of these requirements. Key features include an integrated master-slave seed laser design for stable frequency chirping, fiber-coupled acousto-optic modulator (AOM) gated pulse shaping for long-term thermal stability, and customized amplification stages in a rugged, portable enclosure which simplifiy the alignment and maintenance process. The system in this implementation can deliver up to $450$~mJ per arm, chirp rates up to $\sim22$~MHz$/$ns, and arbitrary temporal profiles within $\sim25$~ns to $\sim1$~$\mu$s. This laser system is validated by measuring the neutral number density of an atmospheric plasma jet, and a two-dimensional temperature map is constructed, demonstrating lab-grade diagnostics for field deployment.

summaries.en: The paper presents a compact, portable, dual-colour chirped-pulse laser system delivering up to 450 mJ per arm, chirp rates up to ~22 MHz/ns, and arbitrary temporal profiles from ~25 ns to ~1 µs, validated by measuring the neutral number density of an atmospheric plasma jet and constructing a two-dimensional temperature map for field-deployable coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering diagnostics.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种紧凑、便携的双色啁啾脉冲激光系统，每路输出能量高达450 mJ，啁啾率可达约22 MHz/ns，并可在约25 ns至约1 µs范围内实现任意时间波形，通过测量大气等离子体射流的中性粒子数密度并构建二维温度图进行了验证，从而为现场部署的相干瑞利-布里渊散射诊断提供实验室级诊断能力。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、各アームで最大450 mJ、チャープ率約22 MHz/ns、約25 nsから約1 µsの任意の時間波形を実現するコンパクトで可搬型の二色チャープパルスレーザーシステムを提案し、大気圧プラズマジェットの中性粒子数密度測定と二次元温度マップの構築により検証することで、現場展開可能なコヒーレントレイリー・ブリルアン散乱診断に実験室級の性能をもたらすことを示した。

title: Noise suppression of quantum frequency conversion in thin-film lithium niobate waveguides via adapted poling
abstract: Quantum frequency conversion (QFC) enables optical interfaces between dissimilar quantum systems, but suppressing noise while maintaining high conversion efficiency remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that adapted poling in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguides reduces the pump-power requirement while shifting the dominant noise mechanism and its power scaling. In 2-cm-long waveguides, adapted poling enables maximum conversion efficiency at an on-chip pump power of $19\pm0.8$~mW, reducing the required pump power by 8~dB and the total conversion noise by 14~dB relative to conventional periodic poling at their respective maximum-conversion operating points. Controlled measurements with different pump conditions and device configurations reveal a transition from predominantly quadratic noise scaling in periodically poled devices to predominantly linear scaling in adapted-poling devices. This transition accompanies a shift from noise dominated by cascaded second-harmonic generation and Stokes spontaneous Raman scattering to direct anti-Stokes spontaneous Raman scattering. These results establish adapted poling as an effective approach to suppressing nonlinear noise, enabling low-noise integrated frequency converters for quantum networks.

summaries.en: Adapted poling in thin-film lithium niobate waveguides reduces the pump power required for maximum quantum frequency conversion efficiency by 8 dB and total conversion noise by 14 dB relative to conventional periodic poling, shifting the dominant noise from cascaded second-harmonic generation and Stokes spontaneous Raman scattering to direct anti-Stokes spontaneous Raman scattering with a transition from quadratic to linear noise power scaling.

title: Broadband chiroptical sensing with two-mode subwavelength grating waveguides
abstract: Engineering local optical chirality in planar photonic structures offers a route to selective and enhanced light-matter interactions with chiral media. Here, we introduce periodic dielectric waveguides that support chiral evanescent fields through the interaction of two nearly degenerate waveguide modes. We develop a perturbation theory for such a waveguide covered by a chiral layer, relating chirality-induced modal coupling and propagation-constant corrections to measurable intermodal power conversion and differential transmission. Whereas modal detuning confines the chiral response of a symmetric waveguide to a narrow spectral range, mode hybridization in an asymmetric waveguide creates individual eigenmodes that carry nonzero local chirality over a broad spectral range. We show that modal dichroism in realistic lossy waveguides can produce a significant background differential transmission signal. Such a background, however, can be suppressed by comparing transmission through two asymmetric waveguides with opposite structural asymmetries, allowing the chiral response to be reliably extracted. Together, these findings provide a basis for developing integrated photonic components with locally chiral fields, including waveguides, metasurfaces, and resonators.

summaries.en: The paper develops a perturbation theory showing that asymmetric two-mode subwavelength grating waveguides support locally chiral evanescent fields over a broad spectral range, and that comparing two waveguides with opposite structural asymmetries suppresses background modal dichroism to reliably extract the chiral response for broadband chiroptical sensing.
summaries.zh: 该论文建立了一种微扰理论，表明非对称双模亚波长光栅波导可在宽光谱范围内支持局域手性倏逝场，并通过比较两个结构非对称性相反的波导来抑制背景模二色性，从而可靠提取手性响应，实现宽带手性光学传感。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、非対称な2モードサブ波長グレーティング導波路が広いスペクトル範囲にわたって局所的なキラルなエバネッセント場を支持することを摂動論で示し、逆の構造非対称性をもつ2つの導波路の透過を比較することで背景のモード二色性を抑制し、キラル応答を確実に抽出して広帯域キロプティカルセンシングを可能にすることを報告している。

title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning $\Delta(t)$ and Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ at frequencies $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2=\nu \omega_1$ respectively with $\nu \in \mathbf{Z}$. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$, and $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$ initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.

summaries.en: Using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation and Floquet perturbation theory, the authors show that a driven Rydberg chain with finite blockade exhibits flat-band melting via many-body resonances that resonantly produce nearest-neighbor Rydberg pairs and via virtual processes accessing such pair states, with distinct dynamics for the vacuum, Z2, and Z3 initial states and proposed pair-correlation measurements as an experimental probe.
summaries.zh: 作者利用含时Schrieffer-Wolff变换和Floquet微扰理论证明，在有限阻塞强度的驱动里德堡链中，平带会通过共振产生最近邻里德堡激发对的多体共振以及经由虚过程访问此类对态的机制而融化，真空、Z2和Z3初态表现出不同动力学，并提出以最近邻对关联函数测量作为实验探针。
summaries.ja: 時間依存Schrieffer-Wolff変換とFloquet摂動理論を用いて、有限のブロッケード強度を持つ駆動Rydberg鎖では、最近接Rydberg励起対を共鳴的に生成する多体共鳴と、そのような対状態を経由する仮想過程という二つの機構によりフラットバンドが融解し、真空・Z2・Z3初期状態が異なるダイナミクスを示すこと、および最近接対相関関数の測定が実験的プローブとなることを示した。

title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.

summaries.en: The authors demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of silicon photonic topological superlattices, enabling deterministic control over the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character.
summaries.zh: 作者通过逆向设计硅基光子拓扑超晶格中的非线性光泵浦分布，展示了拓扑纠缠态的可编程制备，在保持拓扑特性的同时实现对所生成纠缠态维度和模式结构的确定性控制。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、シリコンフォトニックトポロジカル超格子の非線形光学ポンプ分布を逆設計することでトポロジカルもつれ状態のプログラマブルな生成を実証し、トポロジカルな性質を保ちながら生成されるもつれ状態の次元性とモード構造を決定論的に制御できることを示した。

title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.

summaries.en: The exponential-SWAP gate, which creates a coherently tunable superposition of identity and SWAP operations, was experimentally realized between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions, with joint characteristic function measurements confirming continuous control of the superposition.
summaries.zh: 研究人员利用自旋无关和自旋相关的分束器相互作用，在囚禁离子的两个玻色运动模式之间实验实现了指数-SWAP门，该门可产生恒等操作与SWAP操作的相干叠加且振幅可连续调节，并通过测量联合特征函数的部分切片验证了叠加态的连续调控。
summaries.ja: スピン非依存およびスピン依存ビームスプリッター相互作用を用いて、トラップイオンの2つのボソン的運動モード間に、恒等操作とSWAP操作のコヒーレントな重ね合わせを連続的に調整可能な指数SWAPゲートを実験的に実現し、結合特性関数の測定により重ね合わせの連続制御を検証した。

title: A Fibre-Integrated SPDC Heralded Single-Photon Source Using Zn-Indiffused PPLN Ridge Waveguides at Telecom Wavelengths
abstract: We demonstrate a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs at telecom wavelengths based on a commercially available Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide incorporated within a Sagnac interferometer. Operating across the full degenerate SPDC spectrum using pump-suppression filtering only, the source exhibits a measured bandwidth of approximately 67 nm. Strong non-classical correlations are observed, with an average two-photon interference visibility of 96.9 +/- 0.2 %, a fidelity to the Phi + Bell state of 78.1 %, and a CHSH Bell parameter of S = 2.501 +/- 0.005. We further explore the effect of increasing source brightness on Bell-state performance, revealing the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics in high-flux operating regimes.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates a fully fibre-integrated telecom-wavelength source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs using a commercial Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide in a Sagnac interferometer, achieving ~67 nm bandwidth with 96.
summaries.zh: 该论文展示了一种全光纤集成的电信波段宽带偏振纠缠光子对源，采用商用锌扩散MgO:PPLN脊形波导并置于萨格纳克干涉仪中，获得了约67 nm的带宽、96.
summaries.ja: 本論文は、商用のZn拡散MgO:PPLNリッジ導波路をサニャック干渉計に組み込んだ全ファイバ集積型の通信波長帯広帯域偏光もつれ光子対源を実証し、約67 nmの帯域幅、96.

title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
abstract: Bayesian inference enables self-consistent plasma parameter inversion in tokamak integrated data analysis by fusing multi-source diagnostics. However, under nonlinear Gaussian likelihoods, finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate typically relies on sampling methods whose high computational overhead precludes real-time plasma control. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Bayesian inversion framework using a Coherent Ising Machine (CIM)-a quantum computing architecture based on coupled degenerate optical parametric oscillators (DOPOs). With native all-to-all connectivity, the CIM directly maps the negative log-posterior potential onto a spin Hamiltonian and leverages quantum vacuum fluctuations for rapid state-space search during pitchfork bifurcation. Validated on plasma current profile inversion for the EAST tokamak, this method achieves a single-run solution time of approximately 1 ms. Although current qubit limits necessitate a block-wise iterative scheme that prevents full real-time execution today, rapidly scaling quantum hardware offers a clear pathway toward real-time tokamak control.

summaries.en: This paper proposes a Bayesian inversion framework that maps the negative log-posterior potential of nonlinear Gaussian likelihoods onto a spin Hamiltonian solved by a Coherent Ising Machine with all-to-all connectivity, achieving approximately 1 ms single-run plasma current profile inversion on the EAST tokamak, though current qubit limits require a block-wise iterative scheme rather than full real-time control.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种贝叶斯反演框架，将非线性高斯似然下的负对数后验势映射为自旋哈密顿量，并利用具有全连接特性的相干伊辛机进行求解，在EAST托卡马克的等离子体电流剖面反演中实现约1毫秒的单次求解，但受当前量子比特数量限制，需采用分块迭代方案，尚无法完全实时控制。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、非線形ガウス尤度における負の対数事後ポテンシャルをスピンハミルトニアンに写像し、全結合型のコヒーレントイジングマシンで解くベイズ反転フレームワークを提案し、EASTトカマクのプラズマ電流分布反転において約1ミリ秒の単一実行解を得たが、現在の量子ビット数の制約によりブロック反復方式が必要で完全なリアルタイム制御には至っていない。

title: Temperature dependence of a warm ensemble based memory on quantum communication rates
abstract: The success of long-distance quantum communication will hinge on quantum repeater nodes equipped with robust and scalable quantum memories. Such memories must possess specific operating characteristics to make these nodes practical. An attractive option for these memory devices is an atomic warm vapor system operating under the conditions of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). These systems are easy to implement and require relatively low equipment overhead. A key metric in atomic-based quantum memory performance is optical depth, as it is closely tied to the strength of light-matter coupling. Here, we simulate and measure the optical depth-based performance of an EIT quantum memory using a warm atomic vapor cell. We then translate the simulated and measured optical depth and efficiency metrics into expected entanglement distribution rates. Our analysis evaluates the feasibility of these memories in optical quantum repeater nodes, which are essential for robust long-distance quantum communication.

summaries.en: The study simulates and measures the optical-depth-based performance of an electromagnetically induced transparency quantum memory in a warm atomic vapor cell and translates these optical depth and efficiency metrics into expected entanglement distribution rates to assess the feasibility of such memories in optical quantum repeater nodes for long-distance quantum communication.
summaries.zh: 该研究模拟并测量了热原子蒸气池中基于电磁诱导透明的量子存储器的基于光学深度的性能，并将这些光学深度和效率指标转化为预期的纠缠分发速率，以评估此类存储器在用于长距离量子通信的光学量子中继节点中的可行性。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、温暖な原子蒸気セルにおける電磁誘起透明性に基づく量子メモリの光学深度に基づく性能をシミュレーションおよび測定し、これらの光学深度と効率の指標を期待されるもつれ分布速度に変換することで、長距離量子通信のための光量子リピータノードにおけるこうしたメモリの実現可能性を評価する。

title: napari-TurboBox: Interactive Multi-Viewer Bounding Box Annotation for AI-Guided Volumetric Bioimaging
abstract: Promptable segmentation models turn one 3D bounding box into an instance mask. Box placement therefore limits how fast microscopy volumes with thousands of objects are annotated. Each box must be checked in several synchronized viewers, but napari-bbox shares no state between viewers. An edit must update every viewer and slows down with more boxes. napari-TurboBox instead holds one shared copy of the boxes for all viewers. In a four-viewer layout, napari-TurboBox needs a few milliseconds per mouse move to update the three slice viewers up to $10^4$ boxes. The same update in napari-bbox leaves the 33 ms budget beyond about $10^3$ boxes and takes 159 ms at $10^4$. Boxes stay axis-aligned and export to COCO and YOLO as per-slice 2D boxes. napari-TurboBox is a pure-Python plugin for napari 0.6.6 to 0.9. The code is available at this https URL under the Apache 2.0 licence, and version 0.1.0 is archived at this https URL on Zenodo.
subjects: Image and Video Processing (eess.IV) ; Quantitative Methods (q-bio.QM)

summaries.en: napari-TurboBox is a pure-Python napari plugin that shares a single synchronized copy of 3D bounding boxes across multiple viewers, keeping interactive box editing within a few milliseconds even with 10^4 boxes and exporting boxes as per-slice COCO and YOLO 2D annotations.
summaries.zh: napari-TurboBox 是一个纯 Python 的 napari 插件，通过在多个查看器之间共享同一份同步的三维边界框，即使在 10^4 个框的情况下也能将交互式编辑保持在几毫秒内，并将框导出为逐切片的 COCO 和 YOLO 二维标注。
summaries.ja: napari-TurboBoxは、複数のビューア間で単一の同期された3Dバウンディングボックスのコピーを共有する純Pythonのnapariプラグインであり、10^4個のボックスでも数ミリ秒で対話的な編集を維持し、ボックスをスライスごとのCOCOおよびYOLOの2Dアノテーションとしてエクスポートします。

title: A Unified Theory of Image Scaling: Point Spread Functions, Discrete Kernels, and Scale-Spaces
abstract: We derive the optically aligned system of image-scaling operators $\mathbf{K}_s$ that reproduces optical zoom (exact zoom-out, canonical zoom-in), by identifying a Huygens-like consistency principle in which each pixel acts as a secondary source. The system is determined in closed form by the camera's point spread function (PSF), itself the operator $\mathbf{K}_0$. The operators compose, $\mathbf{K}_{s'} \circ \mathbf{K}_s = \mathbf{K}_{ss'}$ (with band projection for down-up), and account for both upscaling and downscaling, which form a Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse pair, $\mathbf{K}_{1/s} = \mathbf{K}_s^\dagger$. We show that image scaling, as routinely practiced, is neither optically faithful nor internally consistent; for example, common anti-aliasing rules generally correspond to no camera, and two resizes by a factor of $1/2$ generally do not equal one resize by a factor of $1/4$. Gaussian scale-space kernels cannot be exact finite-aperture PSFs. Gaussian scale-space is an idealized special case of what emerges here: a generalized scale-space for sampled images, derived entirely from camera optics, bidirectional, and not limited to Gaussian kernels. The system goes beyond scaling and supports composable and invertible subpixel geometric transformations. We empirically validate its optical predictions with real captures and noisy optics simulations, and demonstrate its practical impact on the stability of tasks such as super-resolution and classification.
subjects: Image and Video Processing (eess.IV) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

summaries.en: The paper derives a closed-form system of image-scaling operators determined by the camera's point spread function that composes correctly, forms a Moore–Pinverse pair between upscaling and downscaling, and yields a generalized, bidirectional, non-Gaussian scale-space for sampled images, showing that conventional scaling practice is neither optically faithful nor internally consistent.
summaries.zh: 本文推导出一套由相机点扩散函数确定的闭式图像缩放算子系统，其算子可正确复合，上采样与下采样构成Moore-Penrose伪逆对，并为采样图像产生一个完全源于相机光学的、双向的、非高斯的广义尺度空间，同时表明常规缩放实践既不符合光学真实也不内部一致。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、カメラの点拡がり関数によって閉形式で定まる画像スケーリング作用素の体系を導出し、その作用素が正しく合成され、アップスケーリングとダウンスケーリングがMoore-Penrose擬逆対を成し、サンプリング画像に対する双方向かつ非ガウス的な一般化スケール空間を光学から直接与えることを示すとともに、通例のスケーリング実務が光学的に忠実でも内部的に整合的でもないことを明らかにする。

title: Image Moment Estimation for Crowded Datasets
abstract: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is an imaging technique capable of reconstructing high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) structure of biological macromolecules from a set of noisy projection images taken at random viewing directions. The mathematical model for cryo-EM images typically assumes that each image contains exactly one particle, which is centered at the origin. However, many experimental datasets contain particle images which include multiple particles: one central particle and a few crowding particles. This deviation from the model leads to inaccurate estimation of image statistics, such as the low-order image moments. To account for this, we propose a method to estimate image moments while correcting for the effect of crowding particles. This method can be run directly from a set of cryo-EM micrographs with picked particles, and we demonstrate its efficacy on a wide array of synthetic data.
subjects: Image and Video Processing (eess.IV) ; Quantitative Methods (q-bio.QM)

summaries.en: The paper proposes a method to estimate low-order image moments from cryo-EM datasets containing crowded particle images by correcting for the effect of crowding particles, and demonstrates its efficacy on extensive synthetic data.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种方法，通过校正拥挤粒子的影响，从包含多粒子拥挤图像的冷冻电镜数据集中估计低阶图像矩，并在大量合成数据上验证了其有效性。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、複数の粒子を含む混雑した画像からなるクライオ電子顕微鏡データセットにおいて、混雑粒子の影響を補正しながら低次画像モーメントを推定する手法を提案し、多数の合成データでその有効性を実証している。

title: Spatiotemporal Adaptive Eigenspectrum Remapping in Transcranial Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
abstract: Clutter suppression is a critical preprocessing step in ultrasound blood flow imaging, yet conventional singular value decomposition (SVD) filtering depends on data-specific eigenvalue cutoffs that can remove slow flow along with tissue clutter. Here, we introduce adaptive eigenspectrum remapping (AER), a general framework in which clutter is suppressed by continuously remapping, rather than truncating, the eigenvalue spectrum of the spatiotemporal covariance, and we investigate zero-phase component analysis (ZCA) matrix whitening as an instance of AER for transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM). Rather than discarding eigenspaces, ZCA-based AER whitens the eigenvalue spectrum, reducing the dominance of coherent clutter, including skull reverberation, while retaining weak flow signals. We evaluate AER on both temporal and spatial covariance matrices in mouse brain datasets acquired with long temporal ensembles. Compared with SVD filtering, ZCA improves microbubble contrast and vascular image quality, increases trajectory density across low- and high-concentration regimes, and reveals more low-velocity trajectories in ULM velocity maps. Spatial AER further maintains reconstruction quality across extended ensembles and enables fuller single capillary reporter (SCaRe) reconstructions, including connected artery-to-capillary-to-vein tracks. These results support AER, here instantiated as ZCA whitening, as a data-adaptive alternative to manually thresholded SVD filtering for high-resolution microvascular imaging.
subjects: Image and Video Processing (eess.IV) ; Signal Processing (eess.SP); Medical Physics (physics.med-ph)

summaries.en: Adaptive eigenspectrum remapping (AER), instantiated as zero-phase component analysis whitening, suppresses clutter by remapping rather than truncating the spatiotemporal covariance eigenspectrum, improving microbubble contrast, trajectory density, and low-velocity flow detection in transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy compared with SVD filtering.
summaries.zh: 自适应特征谱重映射（AER）以零相位成分分析白化为实例，通过重映射而非截断时空协方差特征谱来抑制杂波，相比SVD滤波在经颅超声定位显微中提高了微泡对比度、轨迹密度和低速血流检测能力。
summaries.ja: 適応固有スペクトル再マッピング（AER）は、ゼロ位相成分分析ホワイトニングとして実装され、時空間共分散の固有スペクトルを切り捨てるのではなく再マッピングすることでクラッタを抑圧し、SVDフィルタリングと比較して経頭蓋超音波局在顕微鏡におけるマイクロバブルコントラスト、トラジェクトリ密度、低流速血流の検出を向上させる。
